title: Attending Weddings
summary: We talked about weddings we have been to and learned wedding words like ceremony, reception and bride. We listened to stories about unusual weddings and practised showing interest with echo questions and short reactions. We also compared wedding customs around the world.

grammar.title: Showing interest: echo questions and short reactions
grammar.explain: When someone tells us a story, we can repeat a key word as a short question to show interest or surprise. We can also use short auxiliary questions like 'Did you?' or 'Was it?'. Say them with a rising voice so you sound interested.
grammar.explain_ar: عندما يحكي لنا شخص قصة، يمكننا أن نكرّر كلمة مهمة على شكل سؤال قصير لنُظهر الاهتمام أو الدهشة (سؤال الصدى). ويمكننا أيضاً استخدام أسئلة قصيرة بالفعل المساعد مثل Did you? أو Was it?. نقولها بنبرة صاعدة حتى نبدو مهتمّين.
form: Repeat a key word or phrase + ? (rising voice): 'A church hall?'
Statement word order + ? : 'You did the washing up?'
Auxiliary + pronoun + ? (same tense as the speaker): 'Did you?' / 'Was it?' / 'Is she?'
Short reactions: Really? / Oh no! / You're joking!

examples.en: B: He booked a small church hall. A: A church hall?
examples.note: Repeating the surprising words shows interest.

examples.en: A: Really? He worked on his wedding day.
examples.note: Surprise at the groom doing the catering.

examples.en: A: I went to a wedding near Bristol. B: Did you? Whose wedding was it?
examples.note: 'went' is past simple, so the echo uses 'did'.

examples.en: A: It was much cheaper than a normal wedding. B: Was it?
examples.note: 'was' in the story, 'was' in the question.

examples.en: A: The wrong music started playing. B: Oh no!
examples.note: A short reaction encourages the speaker to continue.

mistakes.wrong: A: I went to my cousin's wedding. B: Do you?
mistakes.right: A: I went to my cousin's wedding. B: Did you?
mistakes.why: Use the same tense as the speaker: went → did.

mistakes.wrong: A: She's getting married. B: Does she?
mistakes.right: A: She's getting married. B: Is she?
mistakes.why: The speaker used 'is', so the echo question uses 'is'.

mistakes.wrong: A: They had a civil wedding. B: Had they?
mistakes.right: A: They had a civil wedding. B: Did they?
mistakes.why: 'had' here is the main verb in the past simple, so use 'did'.
A flat voice sounds bored; a rising voice sounds interested.

quiz.q: A: I went to Andy's wedding last week. B: ___? Was it nice?
quiz.why: 'went' is past simple, so the echo question is 'Did you?'.

quiz.q: A: The bride was really nervous. B: ___?
quiz.why: The speaker used 'was', so we use 'was'.

quiz.q: A: My sister is getting married in June. B: ___? That's great!
B: He booked a small church hall. A: ___
quiz.why: Repeat the key words as a question to show interest.

quiz.q: How should you say an echo question to sound interested?
quiz.why: Rising intonation shows interest and surprise.

quiz.q: A: They did all the washing up themselves. B: ___
quiz.why: 'did' (past) → 'They did?' shows surprise in the right tense.
